evidence: Plan: 'flagging any function whose body contains a recognised env read but whose name is not in KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS ... Note the second option would have caught b00f exactly.'

gen_env_registry.py:87-102 defines BULK_ENVIRON_ATTRS (os.environ.copy/items/keys/... register NOTHING); a helper that only calls os.environ.copy() to build a child-process env legitimately reads the environment but names no variable — a body-level 'contains an env read' heuristic would flag it as an unregistered key-bearing helper (FALSE POSITIVE, violating AC #3).

A new shim that delegates to an already-registered helper (e.g. wraps _llm_int) rather than touching os.environ directly would NOT contain a syntactic os.environ read, so a one-level body scan would walk past it (FALSE NEGATIVE) — the very 'wrote a new shim and forgot the row' case the sketch claims to catch.

Non-_llm_ helpers (_env_int, _str_env, _rebar_env, _str_pref, _int_pref, _int_env, _severities_env) live outside config.py and are not covered by the existing _llm_-only guard in test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py.

findings.location: Problem section, 'Why it is harder than the os.environ half' (sketch #2) and Acceptance Criteria #3

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the Problem/Why-it-is-harder framing with scripts/check_config_ownership.py's existing `_shim_access`/`_SHIM_RE` fail-closed detection: state precisely which helper shapes still fail open (e.g. non-`_SHIM_RE`-matching names, or helpers whose literal arg is not `_ENV_NAME_RE`-shaped) rather than asserting the whole helper half 'still fails OPEN'.
evidence: scripts/check_config_ownership.py:448-456 `_shim_access` returns `self._unresolved(node, lit)` for a shim-named callee not in KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS with an _ENV_NAME_RE literal
Plan Sketch #2: 'flagging any function whose ... name is not in KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS' — already implemented by _shim_access
tests/scripts/*seam_clean_heldout.py assert the gate reports zero findings across many source files
findings.finding: The plan's load-bearing premise that the helper half 'still fails OPEN' / 'an unknown helper is silent' / a fix 'has to invent that signal' is refuted by scripts/check_config_ownership.py, which already imports KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS and implements sketch option #2: _shim_access (lines 448-456) uses _SHIM_RE = r'^_.*(env|pref|getenv)' (line 90) to emit an 'unresolved-env-read' finding on a helper-shaped name absent from KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS that passes an env-name-shaped literal. This is a repo-wide gate exercised by ~40 heldout seam-clean tests. A partial fail-closed compensating signal for helper shims therefore already exists.
findings.location: Problem section ('The OTHER half ... still fails OPEN'); 'Why it is harder' section ('Any fix has to invent that signal', Sketch option 2)
scenarios: A new shim named e.g. `_foo_env` with a literal env-name arg would already be flagged by the config-ownership gate, so the premise 'invisible everywhere' is false for that shape.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the premise to scope the gap to what actually escapes _shim_access (a helper whose name does NOT match `^_.*(env|pref|getenv)`, or whose env-name arg is not an ALL-CAPS literal), and note that the generator itself — as distinct from the config-ownership gate — remains fully fail-open on helpers.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend AC #1's escape condition to name scripts/check_config_ownership.py's `_shim_access`/`_SHIM_RE` as a SECOND guard the test helper shape must escape (or be attributed to), so a RED result isolates the generator gap rather than the pre-existing config-ownership shim detector.
evidence: AC #1: 'using a helper shape that escapes the EXISTING guard in tests/unit/test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py'
scripts/check_config_ownership.py:451 `if func.id in KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS or not _SHIM_RE.search(func.id): return None` — shim-named helpers with a literal env-name are flagged
Existing-coverage section names check_config_ownership.py as an oracle but only warns it 'bit the sibling twice', not that its _shim_access already detects unregistered shims
findings.finding: AC #1 requires the AC-#1 test helper to 'escape the EXISTING guard in tests/unit/test_env_registry_helper_coverage.py' but does not require it to also escape (or account for) scripts/check_config_ownership.py's `_shim_access`. Because that gate already fires on shim-named helpers not in KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS, a naive helper shape chosen for the AC-#1 test may already be caught by the config-ownership oracle (not the generator), so a RED result would not prove the generator gap this ticket targets.
scenarios: Author picks helper name `_read_thing_env('REBAR_X')`; it trips _shim_access in the config-ownership gate, muddying which layer produced the RED and whether the generator (the ticket's subject) actually changed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC #1: 'and the shape must be attributable to the GENERATOR, not to check_config_ownership.py::_shim_access — e.g. a non-_SHIM_RE-named helper, verified RED against the generator specifically.'
